back: A disease-causing micro-organism: bacterium, virus, protozoan or fungus.
Infectious: caused by a pathogen that invades the body. Contagious: an infectious disease spread by contact. Tetanus is infectious but not contagious.
An organism (usually a tick or biting fly) that carries a pathogen from one animal to another.
Quarantine: holding new or exposed, apparently healthy animals apart. Isolation: separating animals that are already sick.
Contact, air, feed and water, vectors, equipment and footwear, carriers, animal products, mother to young.
Dung and dirt shield pathogens and weaken disinfectants.
All animals in a house arrive and leave together; the empty house is cleaned, disinfected and rested before the next batch.
Concentrate = total volume ÷ (n + 1); water = the rest.

front: Safe disposal of a carcass after infectious disease
back: Deep burial with lime or burning, away from water; never open a suspected anthrax carcass.
